description: Astral Express is a team of young minds from Yangon, Myanmar, focused on astrophysics, human exploration, Mars, and planetary science. In NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, our goal is to tell the stories and make a presentation about abandoned rovers left behind in space. Through this presentation and data visualizations, we want to remind the world that none of these missions were launched for no purpose. Every piece of hardware should be remembered for fulfilling its purpose.
summary: We developed a website for Challenge Number 1, “Abandoned But Not Forgotten.” In the website we have interactive timelines, mini quizzes, and information about the rovers on the Moon and Mars. We chose this challenge because we thought that it was unfair for the abandoned rovers to be forgotten after their mission has been completed. Our project should make it easy and fun to learn about space exploration and rover missions.
details: Our website includes mini quizzes, timelines about rover missions, and vivid descriptions about rovers in detail. Our features include two interactive planets (Mars and Moon), pages that show images and information in detail about the rover and its properties. Many quizzes about these rovers (24 Questions, 4 questions each rover.) A page where it includes the data that we used from NASA and all citations. (All of our information and data are from NASA sources.)  Hopefully, our project helps new space enthusiasts and kids to learn more about the rovers and the reason why they did not go to waste. Information and data are written in a way to keep it simple and easy to understand. The quizzes are organized in a way to make it fun to learn about rover missions. Our applications/tools include Gemini - Assisting with coding and bug fixes, Figma - For Website Ui, Visual Studio Code - For coding the website, GitHub - For making the website live, Canva and Capcut - For video editing. The language we used is HTML. We used a 3D interactable globe instead of a 2D image for the Mars and Moon. Custom fonts make the website seem lively and fun. After you answer 4 correct questions, there is a confetti effect to congratulate you. Our team decided to make a website that is fun, interactive, easy to understand and a website that contains real and verifiable information by NASA. We chose to only include images and information from NASA, because we thought it would make the website more accurate.
